lessons.titleZh: 離開身邊熟悉的人

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Moving means leaving behind familiar people.

brief.meaningEn: Move away from people whose presence and relationships have become familiar.
brief.meaningZh: 搬離或離開那些原本在身邊、關係已熟悉的人。
brief.grammar: leave familiar people behind / leave behind familiar people; left/leaving; the object can occur before or after behind in this transitive separation use
brief.boundaryZh: 實際離開身邊，不自動表示故意拋棄、背叛或從此斷聯；這與因跟不上進展而 feel left behind 的用法不同。
brief.misconceptionZh: 實際離開身邊，不自動表示故意拋棄、背叛或從此斷聯；這與因跟不上進展而 feel left behind 的用法不同。
brief.outcomeZh: 理解「離開身邊熟悉的人」的語境及用法，並在新情境寫出自然句子。

listening.en: Taking the job in another town meant leaving familiar people behind, especially the neighbours I saw each morning; I still wanted to call them, but knew the everyday encounters would change.
listening.zh: 接受另一城鎮的工作，意味着離開身邊熟悉的人，尤其每天早上見到的鄰居；我仍想打電話給他們，但知道日常相遇會改變。
listening.promptZh: 先只聽示範句。說話者想表達甚麼？

options.en: 說話者要離開平常見面的人，但仍有保持聯絡的意願。
說話者只改了職銜，住處和每天見面的人完全照舊。
說話者決定不再回覆任何舊鄰居的聯絡。
鄰居因跟不上工作進展，被排除在新的培訓外。

listening.explanationZh: another town/everyday encounters 說實際分隔，still call 不表示斷聯；不是進展落後的意思。

reply.promptEn: What made taking the job emotionally difficult?
reply.promptZh: 接受那份工作，在感情上有甚麼難處？

options.en: It meant leaving familiar people behind, including neighbours who were part of each morning.
options.zh: 那意味着離開身邊熟悉的人，包括每天早晨都會遇見的鄰居。

options.en: The ordinary encounters I valued would no longer happen in the same way.
options.zh: 我珍惜的日常相遇，不會再以同樣方式發生。

options.en: Calling people could preserve contact, but would not be the same as seeing them in the street.
options.zh: 電話可以保持聯絡，但跟在街上見面不一樣。

options.en: I had to recognise a change in the relationships around my everyday routine.
options.zh: 我需要承認，自己日常作息周圍的人際接觸會有改變。

reply.explanationZh: 四種回應都能回答這個問題；含有本課表達的回應另外獲得金句標記。

scene.promptZh: 人物只改了同一辦公室內的職銜，仍坐原位、每天跟原同事工作，也沒搬家。介紹想用「離開熟悉的人」形容這次變化。哪句最謹慎？

options.en: The title change alone does not establish that she is leaving familiar people behind.
options.zh: 單憑職銜改變，不能確立她正在離開身邊熟悉的人。

options.en: The new title is a report that she has moved away from the colleagues she knows.
options.zh: 新職銜是在報告她已搬離熟悉同事。

options.en: The account describes her replacing the old daily contacts with an unfamiliar team.
options.zh: 這份敘述說她以陌生團隊取代了原來每日接觸的人。

scene.explanationZh: 要看實際接觸有沒有分隔；這裏工作位置與同事仍在，不能用角色名稱替代人際變化。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種推論不宜由 leaving familiar people behind 的搬離語境得出？

options.en: 日常身邊的人際接觸可能改變。
當事人已決定從此不再跟那些人聯絡。
仍可同時保持電話或其他來往。

contrast.explanationZh: 地理分隔不直接等於主動斷絕關係。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說你仍打算打電話，就不應覺得搬離鄰居有損失；你想說清兩種接觸不同。哪句最好？

options.en: Leaving familiar people behind can change the ordinary moments, even when I keep calling; both kinds of contact matter to me.
options.zh: 即使仍打電話，離開熟悉的人也會改變平常相遇；兩種接觸對我都重要。

options.en: I thought planning calls meant the daily street encounters would remain the same.
options.zh: 我以為計劃打電話，便表示每天街上的相遇會保持不變。

options.en: I would compare only the number of messages, rather than what changes in the way we meet.
options.zh: 我只會比較訊息數量，不看見面方式改變了甚麼。

dialogue.explanationZh: 承認聯絡仍在，也說明日常接觸的不同，不以一項取代另一項。

speaking.en: Leaving familiar people behind does not mean I want to end the relationships, but I know the ordinary ways we meet will change.
speaking.zh: 離開身邊熟悉的人，不表示我想結束關係，但我知道平常見面的方式會改變。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再分身邊接觸改變與關係斷絕。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你剛到新區，一位鄰居邀你參加街坊讀書會。你仍想念搬離前常見的人，但也想開始認識這裏，想問能否先參加一次，不要求新鄰居取代舊關係。用一至兩句英文回覆邀請。

examples.en: Moving here meant leaving familiar people behind, but I would also like to begin getting to know this neighbourhood. Could I join one meeting first and hear what the group enjoys reading?
examples.zh: 搬來這裏，意味着離開身邊熟悉的人，但我也想開始認識這個社區。我可否先參加一次聚會，聽大家喜歡讀甚麼？

examples.en: I have left familiar people behind in my old district, and I miss the everyday conversations. Thank you for inviting me; I would like to try the reading group while keeping those earlier connections too.
examples.zh: 我已離開舊區身邊熟悉的人，也想念平常談話。謝謝你邀請；我想試參加讀書會，同時也保持以前的連繫。

writing.selfCheckZh: 承認搬離後的想念，也回應新的邀請並提出小試；不把新舊關係說成只能選一邊，也不要求別人立即補上所有熟悉感。

takeaways.en: She was leaving familiar people behind when she moved for the course, so she asked which weekly conversations they wanted to keep.
takeaways.zh: 她為課程搬走，要離開身邊熟悉的人，所以先問大家想保留哪些每周談話。

takeaways.en: They left familiar people behind in the old village, but the shared recipe book gave them something to discuss on later calls.
takeaways.zh: 他們離開了舊村身邊熟悉的人，但共用食譜簿給了後來通話時可一起談的事。

lessons.titleZh: 熟悉日常帶來的平和慰藉

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: He missed the quiet comfort of his old street.

brief.meaningEn: Gentle, unobtrusive reassurance or ease, often supplied by familiar things or relationships.
brief.meaningZh: 溫和、不張揚的安慰或安心感，常來自熟悉事物或關係。
brief.grammar: the quiet comfort of a familiar street/routine; find/take quiet comfort in something. Quiet describes the understated feeling, not necessarily complete physical silence.
brief.boundaryZh: 平和慰藉不表示所有問題已解，也不必環境完全無聲；需說哪種熟悉感讓當事人較安心。
brief.misconceptionZh: 平和慰藉不表示所有問題已解，也不必環境完全無聲；需說哪種熟悉感讓當事人較安心。
brief.outcomeZh: 理解「熟悉日常帶來的平和慰藉」的語境及用法，並在新情境寫出自然句子。

listening.en: I missed the quiet comfort of the shopkeeper greeting me by name each morning; the new street was pleasant, but those small recognitions were not part of my day yet.
listening.zh: 我想念店主每天早上叫我名字問好時帶來的平和慰藉；新街道很宜人，但那些小小的熟悉招呼還未成為我的日常。
listening.promptZh: 先只聽示範句。說話者想表達甚麼？

options.en: 說話者想念熟悉招呼帶來的安心感，並非全盤否定新街道。
說話者最在意新街道的噪音，並沒有想念店主的問候。
新街道的店主已每天叫出說話者名字，沒有差別。
說話者只在比較兩條街的租金，沒有提熟悉感。

listening.explanationZh: greeting name/small recognitions 說熟悉感，pleasant new street 保留對新地方的正面評價。

reply.promptEn: What did you miss about the old street?
reply.promptZh: 你想念舊街道的甚麼？

options.en: I missed the quiet comfort of being recognised in the ordinary morning routine.
options.zh: 我想念平常早晨被人認得的平和慰藉。

options.en: The shopkeeper’s familiar greeting made the street feel reassuring.
options.zh: 店主熟悉的招呼，令街道有安心感。

options.en: A small daily recognition had become something I could rely on emotionally.
options.zh: 每天一點被認得的感覺，成了我心裏熟悉的依靠。

options.en: I missed that understated sense of knowing and being known, not a perfect place with no problems.
options.zh: 我想念那種不張揚的熟悉彼此，不是一個毫無問題的完美地方。

reply.explanationZh: 四種回應都能回答這個問題；含有本課表達的回應另外獲得金句標記。

scene.promptZh: 人物在熱鬧早餐桌聽家人熟悉的玩笑，說有溫和安心感；同伴只因環境不安靜，就否定這個 comfort 用法。哪句較準確？

options.en: The familiar jokes can offer quiet comfort even when the room is lively.
options.zh: 即使房間熱鬧，熟悉玩笑仍可帶來不張揚的安心感。

options.en: The noise establishes that the person did not find any reassurance in the breakfast.
options.zh: 聲音熱鬧，已足以證明人物沒有從早餐得到安心感。

options.en: The account describes a silent meal without conversation or laughter.
options.zh: 這份敘述說的是沒有談話或笑聲的無聲用餐。

scene.explanationZh: quiet 可描述慰藉溫和，不要求物理環境完全無聲；應依當事人的感受。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種推論不宜由 quiet comfort 得出？

options.en: 有一種溫和而不張揚的安心感。
實際環境一定完全沒有聲音。
可用熟悉招呼或小習慣說明感受來源。

contrast.explanationZh: 形容感受的quiet，與環境分貝不是同一件事。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說新街道也漂亮，你就不應再想念舊招呼；你想解釋自己不是在比美。哪句最好？

options.en: The quiet comfort came from being recognised, not from judging which street looked better.
options.zh: 那份平和慰藉來自被人認得，不是評哪條街較好看。

options.en: I thought a pleasant appearance would give the same familiarity as years of ordinary greetings.
options.zh: 我以為外觀宜人，就會有跟多年平常招呼一樣的熟悉感。

options.en: I thought missing a place mainly meant being dissatisfied with how the new buildings looked.
options.zh: 我以為想念一個地方，主要表示不滿新建築的外觀。

dialogue.explanationZh: 外觀與熟悉關係的感受不同，可欣賞新街，也想念舊招呼。

speaking.en: There is quiet comfort in a familiar greeting, even when the rest of the day still holds things I need to learn.
speaking.zh: 熟悉招呼裏有一份平和慰藉，即使一天之中仍有許多事需要學。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說熟悉感與仍需適應的事。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你到外地住一學期，想請家人寄來一本自己常讀、旁邊有舊筆記的詩集。它不是貴重收藏，但熟悉的文字讓你在陌生日常裏感到安心。用一至兩句英文提出寄書請求並解釋原因，不要求家人替你解決整段適應生活。

examples.en: Could you send the poetry book with my old notes in the margins? The quiet comfort of those familiar lines would mean more to me here than a new expensive edition.
examples.zh: 你可否寄來那本頁邊有我舊筆記的詩集？在這裏，熟悉詩句帶來的平和慰藉，對我比昂貴新版更有意義。

examples.en: I would love the quiet comfort of reading my annotated poetry book during this unfamiliar term. If it is possible, could you post that copy rather than buy a replacement?
examples.zh: 這學期環境陌生，我很想感受讀那本有自己註記的詩集所帶來的平和慰藉。如果可以，你可否寄來那一本，而不是另買替代？

writing.selfCheckZh: 提出實際寄書請求，以熟悉文字而非價格解釋慰藉；不把一本書說成解決所有適應需要。

takeaways.en: She found quiet comfort in the familiar sound of her uncle making tea while she worked on the difficult letter.
takeaways.zh: 寫那封難開口的信時，叔叔泡茶的熟悉聲音，讓她得到平和慰藉。

takeaways.en: The old recipe offered quiet comfort on the first evening, even though the new kitchen still felt unfamiliar.
takeaways.zh: 第一晚，舊食譜帶來平和慰藉，即使新廚房仍讓人陌生。

lessons.titleEn: the emotional gap after a move
lessons.titleZh: 搬家後心裏留下的空缺

target.pattern: \bthe emotional gap (?:after a move|that comes after it)\b

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: The move itself was easy; the emotional gap that comes after it was harder.
sources.expression: the emotional gap that comes after it

brief.meaningEn: A felt absence or loss of familiar connection following a move, distinct from the practical work of relocation.
brief.meaningZh: 搬家後因熟悉連繫減少而感到的空缺，與實際搬運安排不同。
brief.grammar: the emotional gap after a move; the emotional gap that comes after it requires it to refer clearly to the move; gap is a feeling of missing connection, not a measured physical distance
brief.boundaryZh: 可能在搬得很順利後仍想念，也不表示每人都有相同感受或一定後悔搬家；需說誰缺少哪種連繫。
brief.misconceptionZh: 可能在搬得很順利後仍想念，也不表示每人都有相同感受或一定後悔搬家；需說誰缺少哪種連繫。
brief.outcomeZh: 理解「搬家後心裏留下的空缺」的語境及用法，並在新情境寫出自然句子。
brief.sourceClassificationNote: Creative emotional-absence metaphor. The move is the antecedent of it in the source, so learner wording can name it directly.

listening.en: The boxes were easy to arrange, but the emotional gap after a move surprised me: I no longer had the evening walk with my old neighbour, and had not yet found someone to share those ordinary stories with.
listening.zh: 箱子很容易整理，但搬家後心裏的空缺讓我意外；我不再跟舊鄰居晚間散步，也還未找到可分享那些日常故事的人。
listening.promptZh: 先只聽示範句。說話者想表達甚麼？

options.en: 搬運整理順利，卻仍缺少原有的日常陪伴。
說話者主要不滿箱子放不下，沒有提人際接觸。
說話者已找到完全相同的晚間散步伙伴。
舊鄰居跟說話者一起搬進新住所，每晚仍照舊同行。

listening.explanationZh: boxes easy/but no evening walk 對比物流與熟悉陪伴；尚未有新分享對象，不表示已後悔搬家。

reply.promptEn: What felt difficult even after the boxes were arranged?
reply.promptZh: 箱子整理好後，仍有甚麼讓你覺得難？

options.en: Coping with the emotional gap after a move was harder than arranging the boxes.
options.zh: 應付搬家後心裏的空缺，比安排箱子更難。

options.en: I missed an ordinary way of sharing the day with someone familiar.
options.zh: 我想念跟熟悉的人分享一天的平常方式。

options.en: The practical jobs were done, but the usual companionship was not there.
options.zh: 實際工作做完了，平常的陪伴卻不在。

options.en: I had not yet found a place for those small daily stories in my new routine.
options.zh: 我還未在新作息裏找到分享日常小事的位置。

reply.explanationZh: 四種回應都能回答這個問題；含有本課表達的回應另外獲得金句標記。

scene.promptZh: 人物已認識新同學，但說仍想念舊鄰居的晚間散步；朋友只按新認識的人數，就說原有空缺肯定消失。哪句較準確？

options.en: New contacts do not by themselves show that the emotional gap after a move has disappeared for her.
options.zh: 新接觸本身，不能顯示搬家後心裏的空缺對她已消失。

options.en: The number of new classmates is enough to establish that she no longer misses the old walks.
options.zh: 新同學人數已足以證明她不再想念舊散步。

options.en: She has described the new classmates taking part in the same evening routine with her.
options.zh: 她已描述新同學跟她一起參與相同的晚間習慣。

scene.explanationZh: 看她實際描述的缺少與陪伴，不用新名字數量代情感狀態，也不補出已有相同習慣。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種推論不宜由 the emotional gap after a move 得出？

options.en: 當事人可能缺少熟悉的連繫。
當事人必定認為搬家是錯誤決定。
實際搬運順利與心裏想念可以並存。

contrast.explanationZh: 想念不直接等於否定整個搬家選擇。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說箱子都安好了，再說想念只是小題大做；你想說清自己缺少的事。哪句最好？

options.en: The emotional gap after a move is about the companionship I miss, not whether I have finished putting the boxes away.
options.zh: 搬家後心裏的空缺，是我想念陪伴，不是箱子有沒有收好。

options.en: I thought finishing the practical tasks meant the familiar company would already have a place in the new routine.
options.zh: 我以為實際工作完了，熟悉陪伴就已在新作息裏有位置。

options.en: I think a better storage arrangement would address the main loss I have described.
options.zh: 我認為更好的收納安排，會回應自己所說的主要失落。

dialogue.explanationZh: 區分物件安排與關係日常，先聽具體缺少，不只再添收納。

speaking.en: I want to describe the emotional gap after a move without suggesting that I regret every part of the choice.
speaking.zh: 我想描述搬家後心裏的空缺，不暗示自己後悔這個選擇的每一部分。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再分想念與全盤後悔。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你寫一篇搬家隨筆，編輯把標題擬成「後悔離開」。你其實仍高興選了新課程，只是想念舊街道的日常談話。你想請標題保留心裏空缺，也保留自己仍支持這個選擇的部分，不把想念寫成全盤後悔。用一至兩句英文向編輯說明。

examples.en: The emotional gap after a move is real for me, but it does not mean I wish I had rejected the new course. Could the title leave room for both missing the old conversations and valuing the choice I made?
examples.zh: 搬家後心裏的空缺對我是真實的，但不表示我希望當初拒絕新課程。標題可否同時容納想念舊談話，以及珍惜自己選擇這兩部分？

examples.en: I am describing the emotional gap after a move, not a verdict that leaving was a mistake. I would like the heading to keep my continued interest in the course alongside the familiar company I miss.
examples.zh: 我在描述搬家後心裏的空缺，不是判定離開是錯誤。我希望標題保留自己仍對課程有興趣，也保留想念熟悉陪伴的部分。

writing.selfCheckZh: 向編輯說清兩種感受並存，提出與原文相符的標題範圍；不把想念升格成全盤後悔，也不為保留正面選擇抹去空缺。

takeaways.en: The emotional gap after a move became clear when she reached for the phone to share the day’s news with a neighbour who no longer lived next door.
takeaways.zh: 她伸手想打電話給已不再住隔壁的鄰居，分享當天消息時，搬家後心裏的空缺變得清楚。

takeaways.en: He wrote about the move and the emotional gap that comes after it, especially the missing afternoon conversations in the shared garden.
takeaways.zh: 他寫到搬家以及之後心裏的空缺，尤其想念共用花園裏的下午談話。

lessons.titleZh: 在社區建立深厚連繫

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Over time, families can build deep roots in a town.

brief.meaningEn: Develop strong and lasting connections with a place and its community over time.
brief.meaningZh: 隨時間跟地方及其社群建立深厚、持久的連繫。
brief.grammar: build/built/building deep roots in a town/community; roots evoke sustained ties and deep emphasises their strength
brief.boundaryZh: 深厚連繫不只按住了幾年、出生地或是否擁有物業判斷；需有實際關係與參與，也不表示不能離開探索。
brief.misconceptionZh: 深厚連繫不只按住了幾年、出生地或是否擁有物業判斷；需有實際關係與參與，也不表示不能離開探索。
brief.outcomeZh: 理解「在社區建立深厚連繫」的語境及用法，並在新情境寫出自然句子。
brief.sourceClassificationNote: Productive community-root metaphor, related to putting down roots but foregrounding depth developed over time rather than simply beginning to settle. No separate dictionary sense is claimed for build deep roots.

listening.en: Through years of helping at the garden and asking neighbours about their stories, we built deep roots in the area; people began coming to us with ideas, not just recognising our address.
listening.zh: 多年在園圃幫忙、聽鄰居說故事後，我們在區內建立了深厚連繫；大家開始帶構想來找我們，不只是認得住址。
listening.promptZh: 先只聽示範句。說話者想表達甚麼？

options.en: 持續參與和來往，讓小組與社區有較深互信。
只因地址登記已久，小組從未參與也已獲相同互信。
大家只把小組當未曾見過的外來團隊。
小組收到鄰居構想後，才第一次開始參與園圃工作。

listening.explanationZh: years helping/asking/ideas brought 說關係逐漸加深，不是只按地址，亦不是收到構想後才首次參與。

reply.promptEn: How did you become closely connected with the neighbourhood?
reply.promptZh: 你們怎樣跟社區建立密切連繫？

options.en: We built deep roots through years of taking part and listening to neighbours.
options.zh: 我們多年參與、聆聽鄰居，建立了深厚連繫。

options.en: The garden gave us repeated opportunities to work with people and hear their stories.
options.zh: 園圃給我們反覆跟人合作、聽故事的機會。

options.en: Trust grew through ordinary shared activity, not merely through having an address there.
options.zh: 信任從平常共同活動中增長，不只是因為有個地址。

options.en: People began treating us as someone to approach with ideas after that continuing involvement.
options.zh: 持續參與後，大家開始把我們當作可以帶構想來商量的人。

reply.explanationZh: 四種回應都能回答這個問題；含有本課表達的回應另外獲得金句標記。

scene.promptZh: 你只知道一位人物出生在某城、地址一直在那裏，未有他跟社群來往的資料；朋友直接稱他與社區連繫很深。哪句最謹慎？

options.en: The birthplace and address alone do not show how he has built deep roots in the community.
options.zh: 單憑出生地與住址，不能顯示他怎樣在社區建立了深厚連繫。

options.en: The same address establishes that he regularly joins community work and is trusted with shared plans.
options.zh: 相同地址已足以證明他經常參與社區工作，也獲信任一起規劃。

options.en: The account already describes the neighbours seeking him out for advice.
options.zh: 這份敘述已說鄰居主動找他商量。

scene.explanationZh: 深度需有關係及參與線索，不能由地址補出具體合作或互信。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種推論不宜由 build deep roots in a community 得出？

options.en: 跟社區的連繫可能隨持續參與加深。
沒有在這裏出生的人，就不可能建立深厚連繫。
仍可具體說哪些關係及活動支撐這個比喻。

contrast.explanationZh: 根的比喻不把連繫只留給出生於當地的人。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說新來的人沒有家族歷史，做再多都不算有根；你想指出實際參與的重要。哪句最好？

options.en: People can build deep roots through sustained relationships, even if their families did not start here.
options.zh: 即使家人不是從這裏開始，人也可透過持續關係建立深厚連繫。

options.en: I would use the age of the family address as the main test before considering any shared activity.
options.zh: 我會先把家族地址多久作主要判準，再考慮共同活動。

options.en: I thought roots meant an inherited identity that later relationships could not contribute to.
options.zh: 我以為根只代表承傳身份，之後建立的關係不能加進去。

dialogue.explanationZh: 這個用法重視實際深厚連繫，不把出生或家族年資當唯一資格。

speaking.en: I hope to build deep roots here by taking part consistently, rather than expecting one visit to make every connection.
speaking.zh: 我希望透過持續參與，在這裏建立深厚連繫，不指望一次到訪就有所有關係。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出持續參與的具體方法。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：剛搬來的同學說自己沒有本地親戚，永遠只能當旁觀者。你想邀他自願幫街坊戲劇組整理故事錄音，說這可成為逐漸建立連繫的一步，也容許先來看看，不承諾一次就人人接納。用一至兩句英文邀請。

examples.en: You can begin to build deep roots here without a local family history. If you are interested, would you like to visit the drama group and see whether helping with the story recordings feels like a way to take part?
examples.zh: 即使沒有本地家族歷史，你也可以開始建立深厚連繫。若你有興趣，想不想先看看戲劇組，了解幫忙整理故事錄音是否適合作為參與方式？

examples.en: We do not have to inherit every connection to build deep roots in a place. You could start by meeting the people collecting the recordings, with no pressure to promise a regular role before you have seen the work.
examples.zh: 要在一個地方建立深厚連繫，不必每段關係都是承傳而來。你可先見收集錄音的人，不用在看過工作前就承諾固定角色。

writing.selfCheckZh: 以可自選的小參與回應「永遠旁觀」的想法，強調連繫可逐步建立；不把血緣當唯一資格，也不保證即時接納或代他承諾。

takeaways.en: She built deep roots in the town through years of sharing the library work with people from different streets.
takeaways.zh: 她多年跟不同街道的人一起做圖書館工作，在城鎮建立了深厚連繫。

takeaways.en: They were building deep roots as neighbours began sharing not only requests for help but ideas for the next community event.
takeaways.zh: 鄰居開始不只求助，也分享下次社區活動構想時，他們正在建立深厚連繫。

lessons.titleEn: roots, rhythm, and a stronger sense of home
lessons.titleZh: 連繫、節奏與更深的歸屬感

target.pattern: \broots, rhythm, and a stronger sense of home\b

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Years in one town gave her roots, rhythm, and a stronger sense of home.
sources.expression: roots, rhythm, and a stronger sense of home

brief.meaningEn: A combination of belonging through relationships, familiar routines and increased emotional attachment to a place.
brief.meaningZh: 人際連繫、熟悉作息，以及對地方更強的歸屬感，三者結合。
brief.grammar: a place/time there gave someone roots, rhythm, and a stronger sense of home; the list combines plant and music images with felt belonging
brief.boundaryZh: 不能只按居住年期判定三者都已具備，也不表示必須擁有物業或永不搬走；要給關係、作息與感受的實際線索。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不能只按居住年期判定三者都已具備，也不表示必須擁有物業或永不搬走；要給關係、作息與感受的實際線索。
brief.outcomeZh: 理解「連繫、節奏與更深的歸屬感」的語境及用法，並在新情境寫出自然句子。
brief.sourceClassificationNote: Creative three-part description, not one fixed idiom or a promise that staying always produces belonging. Related root metaphors alone do not express the whole list.

listening.en: The neighbourhood gave me roots, rhythm, and a stronger sense of home through the people I met at the garden, the Saturday market routine and the feeling that someone noticed when I returned.
listening.zh: 透過園圃認識的人、周六街市的習慣，以及回來時有人留意的感覺，這個社區給了我連繫、節奏和更深的歸屬感。
listening.promptZh: 先只聽示範句。說話者想表達甚麼？

options.en: 關係、固定活動與被留意的感受，一起加深了地方的歸屬感。
說話者只因買下物業，便沒有再參與任何日常活動。
歸屬感主要來自一次臨時派對，沒有每周重複的活動或關係。
說話者還未認識任何人，也未有固定習慣。

listening.explanationZh: people/market/noticed 對應三部分，不是只看地址，也不是一次臨時派對。

reply.promptEn: What made the neighbourhood feel more like home?
reply.promptZh: 甚麼讓這個社區更有家的感覺？

options.en: It gave me roots, rhythm, and a stronger sense of home through people, routine and being noticed.
options.zh: 透過人、習慣和被留意，這裏給我連繫、節奏與更深的歸屬感。

options.en: The garden introduced me to people who became part of my ordinary week.
options.zh: 園圃讓我認識的人，成了我平常一周的一部分。

options.en: The market visit became a familiar pattern rather than a place I passed once.
options.zh: 去街市成了熟悉習慣，不是只經過一次的地方。

options.en: Returning mattered because people noticed me and the place felt connected with my life.
options.zh: 回來之所以重要，是有人留意我，這地方跟我的生活有了連繫。

reply.explanationZh: 四種回應都能回答這個問題；含有本課表達的回應另外獲得金句標記。

scene.promptZh: 人物已有固定街市習慣，也認得幾位店主，卻仍明說自己像客人、尚未感到是家；朋友想把三部分都寫成已建立。哪句較謹慎？

options.en: Some parts of roots, rhythm, and a stronger sense of home are emerging, but her stated feeling of belonging still needs to be respected.
options.zh: 連繫、節奏與更深歸屬感之中，有些部分正在形成，但仍要尊重她說自己尚未歸屬的感受。

options.en: The regular market visit establishes that she already feels fully at home.
options.zh: 固定去街市，已足以證明她完全有家的感覺。

options.en: Feeling like a guest means she has not formed any routine or recognised any local person.
options.zh: 感到像客人，表示她沒有形成任何習慣，也不認得任何本地人。

scene.explanationZh: 三部分可不同步形成，不能用其中一項代全部，也不因歸屬未足便否認已有日常。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種推論不宜由 roots, rhythm, and a stronger sense of home 得出？

options.en: 關係、習慣和感受共同構成一種歸屬。
要有這些感受，就必須擁有當地物業而且永不離開。
仍可用個人具體經驗說明，不能只看住了多久。

contrast.explanationZh: 三部分是生活與感受，不是法律產權或永久不搬的條件。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說你將搬走，就不能再感謝這裏曾給你歸屬；你想說明珍惜與改變可並存。哪句最好？

options.en: This place gave me roots, rhythm, and a stronger sense of home; moving does not erase what I learned to value here.
options.zh: 這地方給過我連繫、節奏與更深的歸屬感；搬走不會抹去我在這裏學會珍惜的事。

options.en: I thought a meaningful sense of home required me to keep the same address for the rest of my life.
options.zh: 我以為有意義的歸屬感，要求自己一生保留同一地址。

options.en: I would judge the old routines only by whether I can repeat them exactly in the new place.
options.zh: 我只會按能否在新地方原樣重做，評價舊日常的意義。

dialogue.explanationZh: 已有的意義可保留並改變形式，不以終身住址或完全複製作條件。

speaking.en: I want roots, rhythm, and a stronger sense of home, but I know those feelings need time and real relationships rather than an address alone.
speaking.zh: 我想有連繫、節奏與更深的歸屬感，但知道這些感受需要時間和真實關係，不只是地址。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說歸屬所需的日常與關係。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你將離開住了幾年的街區，想在街坊聚餐說一小段感謝。這裏給過你固定周末活動與互相照應的人，你想帶着這些價值去新地方，也邀舊朋友日後保持來往，不把搬走說成過去毫無根基。用一至兩句英文告別。

examples.en: You have given me roots, rhythm, and a stronger sense of home through our shared weekends and small acts of care. I hope to carry those habits into the next place while keeping a place for these friendships in my life.
examples.zh: 透過共同周末和小小照應，你們給了我連繫、節奏與更深的歸屬感。我希望把這些習慣帶到下一個地方，同時在生活裏保留這些友誼。

examples.en: The years here brought roots, rhythm, and a stronger sense of home, not just a longer list of addresses. Thank you for being part of that; I would like us to keep talking after the move, even as our routines change.
examples.zh: 這幾年帶來的是連繫、節奏與更深的歸屬感，不只是地址清單多了一項。謝謝你們參與其中；即使作息改變，搬走後我仍想跟大家繼續談話。

writing.selfCheckZh: 以具體共處與照應感謝原有歸屬，說明想延續的價值與來往；不把新階段當舊連繫從未存在，也不承諾形式永遠不變。

takeaways.en: The evening choir gave her roots, rhythm, and a stronger sense of home as familiar voices became part of each week.
takeaways.zh: 晚間合唱團的熟悉聲音成了每周一部分，給了她連繫、節奏與更深的歸屬感。

takeaways.en: He found roots, rhythm, and a stronger sense of home in shared breakfasts and the neighbours who began asking how his work was going.
takeaways.zh: 共同早餐，以及開始問他工作近況的鄰居，讓他找到連繫、節奏與更深的歸屬感。

lessons.titleEn: roots can sometimes turn into ruts
lessons.titleZh: 根基也可能變成停滯的慣性

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Without change, roots can sometimes turn into ruts.
sources.expression: roots can sometimes turn into ruts

brief.meaningEn: Established sources of stability can sometimes become limiting habits when people stop adapting.
brief.meaningZh: 原本帶來穩定的根基，有時會變成限制發展、不再調整的慣性。
brief.grammar: roots can sometimes turn into ruts; can/sometimes mark a possibility, not an inevitable result. The similar sounds connect the plant-root and worn-track images.
brief.boundaryZh: 長久、熟悉本身不等於停滯；要有不願調整或未回應新需要的線索，也不必為改變而丟掉所有根基。
brief.misconceptionZh: 長久、熟悉本身不等於停滯；要有不願調整或未回應新需要的線索，也不必為改變而丟掉所有根基。
brief.outcomeZh: 理解「根基也可能變成停滯的慣性」的語境及用法，並在新情境寫出自然句子。
brief.sourceClassificationNote: A creative contrast between established roots and limiting ruts, rather than a separate fixed dictionary idiom.

listening.en: Our neighbourhood routines once helped people feel secure, but roots can sometimes turn into ruts if we stop asking whether the meeting times still suit those who work late.
listening.zh: 社區原有的習慣曾讓人安心，但如果不再問聚會時間是否仍適合晚下班的人，根基有時也會變成停滯的慣性。
listening.promptZh: 先只聽示範句。說話者想表達甚麼？

options.en: 原有習慣可帶來穩定，但不再回應需要時也可能限制參與。
說話者已確定晚下班的人不想參與，所以不用再問。
說話者認為所有長期習慣都應立即取消。
聚會已改成晚間，所有人的意見也已收集完畢。

listening.explanationZh: once secure 承認原有價值，if stop asking 指出可能的僵化條件，並非一律否定熟悉習慣。

reply.promptEn: Why do you want to ask about the meeting times again?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼想再問大家聚會時間的需要？

options.en: Roots can sometimes turn into ruts if we keep a routine without checking whom it now leaves out.
options.zh: 如果保留習慣卻不看現在把誰排除在外，根基有時會變成停滯的慣性。

options.en: A time that suited the original group may not suit people who have joined since.
options.zh: 原先適合小組的時間，不一定適合後來加入的人。

options.en: I value the familiar routine, but want to know whether it still enables people to take part.
options.zh: 我珍惜熟悉習慣，但想知道它是否仍讓大家能夠參與。

options.en: Asking again would help us distinguish useful stability from an arrangement we repeat without thinking.
options.zh: 再問一次，可幫我們分清有用的穩定和未經思考就照做的安排。

reply.explanationZh: 四種回應都能回答這個問題；含有本課表達的回應另外獲得金句標記。

scene.promptZh: 一間老店保持熟悉的招呼方式，也持續試新服務、聽取客人意見；評論只因它開了多年，就說根基已成停滯。哪句較謹慎？

options.en: The shop’s age alone does not show that the warning “roots can sometimes turn into ruts” applies to its present habits.
options.zh: 單憑店舖年資，不能判斷「根基有時會變成停滯慣性」適用於目前的習慣。

options.en: Keeping the familiar greeting establishes that the shop has stopped responding to customers.
options.zh: 保留熟悉招呼，足以確立店舖已不再回應客人。

options.en: Trying new services means the shop no longer has any continuing connection with its earlier customers.
options.zh: 試新服務，表示店舖跟舊客已沒有任何延續的連繫。

scene.explanationZh: 看有沒有調整及回應需要，不能只用年資判停滯，也不能把嘗試新事物當成沒有根基。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種理解不宜由 roots can sometimes turn into ruts 得出？

options.en: 穩定的習慣若不再回應需要，可能變得限制人。
建立深厚關係後，停滯便是無法避免的結果。
可保留有用的根基，同時檢視需要調整的習慣。

contrast.explanationZh: can sometimes 保留條件和可能，並沒有說所有根基必然造成停滯。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說家族活動既然已做多年，就不必再問年輕成員想怎樣參與；你想珍惜傳統也保持開放。哪句最好？

options.en: Roots can sometimes turn into ruts; I would keep the shared stories and ask how younger members want to take part.
options.zh: 根基有時會變成停滯慣性；我會保留共同故事，也問年輕成員想怎樣參與。

options.en: I assumed that repeating the familiar programme was itself enough to show what younger members wanted.
options.zh: 我原以為，只要重複熟悉節目，就足以顯示年輕成員想要甚麼。

options.en: I would replace the shared stories first and ask about participation afterwards.
options.zh: 我會先換掉共同故事，之後才問參與方式。

dialogue.explanationZh: 同時保存連繫和了解需要；熟悉不代替詢問，調整也不一定要先抹去原有內容。

speaking.en: Roots can sometimes turn into ruts when we treat a useful old arrangement as a reason never to hear new questions.
speaking.zh: 當我們把有用的舊安排當成永不聽新問題的理由，根基有時會變成停滯慣性。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說明有價值的穩定怎樣可能變得僵化。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你為家族食譜簿寫序言。你想保留長輩的故事，但也邀新使用者記下份量疑問及實際試做的調整，不把舊寫法當成不能問的規則。用一至兩句英文向讀者說明怎樣使用這本簿。

examples.en: Roots can sometimes turn into ruts if a family recipe book leaves no room for questions. Keep the stories, but please add notes about quantities and the adjustments you try.
examples.zh: 如果家族食譜簿不容提問，根基有時會變成停滯慣性。請保留故事，也記下份量問題及你試過的調整。

examples.en: These recipes connect us with earlier cooks, yet roots can sometimes turn into ruts when we treat every old instruction as untouchable. Please record what you learn as you cook, alongside the family stories.
examples.zh: 這些食譜讓我們跟前人連繫，但若把每條舊指示都視為不能改，根基有時也會變成停滯慣性。請在家族故事旁，記下你實際做菜時學到的事。

writing.selfCheckZh: 對讀者提出可行的記錄方式，同時保留故事與提問空間；不把傳承一概視為問題，也不把試做調整說成背叛。

takeaways.en: The club secretary warned that roots can sometimes turn into ruts when a long-standing rule prevents new members from suggesting an activity.
takeaways.zh: 會務秘書提醒，當長久規則阻止新會員提議活動時，根基有時會變成停滯慣性。

takeaways.en: Their shared history was valuable, but roots can sometimes turn into ruts if the committee mistakes familiarity for evidence that a plan still works.
takeaways.zh: 共同歷史很有價值，但若委員會把熟悉誤當成計劃仍有效的證據，根基有時會變成停滯慣性。

lessons.titleEn: strong roots without becoming afraid to branch out
lessons.titleZh: 有穩固連繫，也敢探索新方向

target.pattern: \bstrong roots without becoming afraid to branch out\b

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Young adults can have strong roots without becoming afraid to branch out.
sources.expression: strong roots without becoming afraid to branch out

brief.meaningEn: Maintain a secure sense of identity or belonging while remaining willing to explore unfamiliar interests or directions.
brief.meaningZh: 保持穩固的身分或歸屬連繫，同時仍願意探索陌生興趣或方向。
brief.grammar: have strong roots without becoming afraid to branch out; branch out into a new activity. Without connects secure foundations with continued openness.
brief.boundaryZh: 有根基與探索新方向可以並存；不表示探索就是背棄原有關係，也不要求所有人採取同一種新嘗試。
brief.misconceptionZh: 有根基與探索新方向可以並存；不表示探索就是背棄原有關係，也不要求所有人採取同一種新嘗試。
brief.outcomeZh: 理解「有穩固連繫，也敢探索新方向」的語境及用法，並在新情境寫出自然句子。
brief.sourceClassificationNote: An extended tree image combining strong roots and branching out, rather than a new fixed meaning for the whole sentence.

listening.en: Joining the student journal did not stop Lea calling her family on Sundays; she wanted strong roots without becoming afraid to branch out into interests they had not shared before.
listening.zh: 加入學生刊物沒有讓 Lea 停止周日給家人打電話；她想保持穩固連繫，也不怕探索家人以前沒有共同參與的興趣。
listening.promptZh: 先只聽示範句。說話者想表達甚麼？

options.en: 她想保持家人連繫，同時探索新的興趣。
她因加入刊物，已決定不再跟家人來往。
她只選家人參與過的活動，避免任何陌生興趣。
家人已全部加入同一刊物，所以她沒有接觸新方向。

listening.explanationZh: Sunday calls 與new interests 同時存在，並非必須在原有關係和新興趣之間二選一。

reply.promptEn: What balance was Lea looking for?
reply.promptZh: Lea 想取得怎樣的平衡？

options.en: She wanted strong roots without becoming afraid to branch out into unfamiliar interests.
options.zh: 她想有穩固連繫，也不怕探索陌生興趣。

options.en: She wanted to stay in touch with her family while trying something new for herself.
options.zh: 她想保持家人聯絡，同時為自己試新事物。

options.en: Her family connections mattered, but did not need to decide every activity she joined.
options.zh: 家人連繫對她重要，但不必決定她參加的每項活動。

options.en: She was seeking both continuity and room to develop interests of her own.
options.zh: 她想同時有延續的連繫，以及發展個人興趣的空間。

reply.explanationZh: 四種回應都能回答這個問題；含有本課表達的回應另外獲得金句標記。

scene.promptZh: 人物珍惜原有朋友圈，卻因怕被當成不忠而拒絕所有陌生興趣；她問這是否已表現出有根基也敢探索。哪句最準確？

options.en: Her existing friendships provide roots, but her fear of trying anything new does not yet show strong roots without becoming afraid to branch out.
options.zh: 原有友誼提供根基，但她害怕試任何新事物，尚未顯示有穩固連繫也不怕探索。

options.en: Declining unfamiliar interests is the part that demonstrates her willingness to explore.
options.zh: 拒絕陌生興趣，正是顯示她願意探索的部分。

options.en: Trying a new interest would itself mean she had stopped valuing her old friends.
options.zh: 只要試新興趣，就表示她不再珍惜舊朋友。

scene.explanationZh: 句子同時要求連繫與開放；恐懼不是探索意願，新活動也不必取消舊友情。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種理解不宜由 strong roots without becoming afraid to branch out 得出？

options.en: 穩固歸屬可以跟新嘗試並存。
只有放棄原有關係，才算真正探索新方向。
不同人可用不同活動保持連繫並發展興趣。

contrast.explanationZh: 這個並置圖像不是要求先拔掉根基才伸展。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說你參加不同藝術領域的合作，就是不再重視原來團體；你想說清仍有連繫，也有探索空間。哪句最好？

options.en: I want strong roots without becoming afraid to branch out; I can keep contributing here and learn from a different collaboration.
options.zh: 我想保持穩固連繫，也不怕探索新方向；我可以繼續在這裏參與，也從不同合作學習。

options.en: I assumed keeping a connection meant choosing only projects this group had already tried.
options.zh: 我原以為，保持連繫就是只選這團體已試過的項目。

options.en: I would leave the original group before finding out whether the two commitments can fit together.
options.zh: 我會先退出原團體，之後才了解兩邊投入能否配合。

dialogue.explanationZh: 說明兩種投入可並存，再了解實際安排，不把陌生合作直接等同不忠。

speaking.en: Our group wants strong roots without becoming afraid to branch out, so the new collaboration will begin with local stories and invite other ways of telling them.
speaking.zh: 我們團體想保持穩固連繫，也不怕探索新方向，所以新合作會從本地故事開始，並邀請其他敘述方式。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說連繫與探索如何一起成立。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你答應為飲食播客示範家傳食譜，也想試不同配料。製作人打算把你介紹成整個文化的代表；你想請他改成你一家的一種做法，既尊重來處，也容許個人探索。用一至兩句英文向製作人提出介紹方式的修改。

examples.en: I want strong roots without becoming afraid to branch out, so I will begin with my grandmother’s recipe and explain the variations I try. Please introduce it as one family’s version, not as the voice of an entire culture.
examples.zh: 我想保持穩固連繫，也不怕探索新方向，所以會從祖母食譜開始，解釋自己試的變化。請把它介紹為一個家庭的版本，而不是整個文化的聲音。

examples.en: For me, having strong roots without becoming afraid to branch out means respecting the recipe’s history while exploring ingredients. Could the introduction say whose family recipe this is, rather than present my choices as what everyone does?
examples.zh: 對我而言，有穩固連繫也不怕探索新方向，是尊重食譜歷史，同時探索配料。介紹可否交代這是誰家的食譜，而不是把我的選擇當成所有人的做法？

writing.selfCheckZh: 向製作人提出具體身分介紹修改，同時交代承傳與個人探索；不讓一個人的版本代表所有人，也不以創新否定來處。

takeaways.en: Her weekly visits to the old neighbourhood helped her keep strong roots without becoming afraid to branch out into work in a different city.
takeaways.zh: 每周回訪舊社區，幫她保持穩固連繫，也不怕探索另一城市的工作。

takeaways.en: The choir encouraged strong roots without becoming afraid to branch out, keeping its shared songs while inviting members to introduce music they had discovered elsewhere.
takeaways.zh: 合唱團鼓勵有穩固連繫也不怕探索新方向，保留共同歌曲，也邀團員介紹在別處發現的音樂。

lessons.titleEn: a fresh page rather than just a new address
lessons.titleZh: 新階段，不只是換了地址

target.pattern: \ba fresh page rather than just a new address\b

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Her relocation felt like a fresh page rather than just a new address.
sources.expression: a fresh page rather than just a new address

brief.meaningEn: A meaningful opportunity for a new stage of life, rather than a change of location alone.
brief.meaningZh: 有意義的新生活階段或機會，而不只是住址改變。
brief.grammar: feel like / offer a fresh page rather than just a new address; page is a writing metaphor, while address names the physical move.
brief.boundaryZh: 搬遷不自動帶來心理轉變；新的開始也不等於抹去過去，需看當事人實際想展開甚麼。
brief.misconceptionZh: 搬遷不自動帶來心理轉變；新的開始也不等於抹去過去，需看當事人實際想展開甚麼。
brief.outcomeZh: 理解「新階段，不只是換了地址」的語境及用法，並在新情境寫出自然句子。
brief.sourceClassificationNote: An extended contrast between a new life chapter and a physical address change; not a fixed dictionary idiom as a whole.

listening.en: Moving nearer the evening college felt like a fresh page rather than just a new address: I could finally begin the course I had postponed, while keeping the friendships that mattered to me.
listening.zh: 搬到夜校附近，感覺是新階段，而不只是換了地址：我終於能開始一直延後的課程，同時保持珍惜的友誼。
listening.promptZh: 先只聽示範句。說話者想表達甚麼？

options.en: 搬遷讓說話者開始想讀的課程，但沒有要求放棄舊友。
說話者只是更改郵寄資料，生活安排和目標都沒有變。
說話者把搬遷當成不再需要以前朋友的理由。
課程在搬家前已修畢，所以搬近學校沒有新機會。

listening.explanationZh: finally begin course 提供新階段的實際內容；keeping friendships 表示不必抹去過去。

reply.promptEn: Why did the move feel significant to you?
reply.promptZh: 這次搬遷為甚麼對你有重要意義？

options.en: It offered a fresh page rather than just a new address, because I could begin a course I had kept postponing.
options.zh: 它帶來新階段，而不只是新地址，因為我能開始一直延後的課程。

options.en: Living nearer the college made a long-delayed plan practical.
options.zh: 住近學校，讓延後已久的計劃變得可行。

options.en: The change mattered because it opened a specific opportunity in my everyday life.
options.zh: 改變之所以重要，是它在日常生活中打開了具體機會。

options.en: I could take a new direction without treating my earlier friendships as something to discard.
options.zh: 我可以走新方向，不必把以前的友誼當成要丟掉的東西。

reply.explanationZh: 四種回應都能回答這個問題；含有本課表達的回應另外獲得金句標記。

scene.promptZh: 人物搬到隔壁街，只為交通方便，明說仍想維持原有工作和計劃。旁人單看新郵政地址，就把它寫成全新人生方向。哪句較謹慎？

options.en: A different address alone does not establish a fresh page rather than just a new address in the person’s own experience.
options.zh: 單有不同地址，不能確立當事人親身感受到新階段而不只是換地址。

options.en: The new postal details show that the person has chosen to replace the earlier goals.
options.zh: 新的郵寄資料顯示當事人已選擇換掉原有目標。

options.en: The person’s stated aim is to replace the old working routine, with the shorter journey only incidental.
options.zh: 當事人已說明的目標是換掉舊工作作息，較短路程只是次要。

scene.explanationZh: 按本人已說的目的分清交通改善與新生活方向，不能由新郵寄資料推斷已更換目標。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種推論不宜由 a fresh page rather than just a new address 得出？

options.en: 新階段可有具體機會作支持。
只要搬家，就已抹去過去的關係與經驗。
當事人可珍惜過去，同時開始新的安排。

contrast.explanationZh: 新頁是展開階段的圖像，不是把過去清除的保證。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說搬家必定意味重塑自己；你想知道對當事人真正重要的是甚麼。哪句最好？

options.en: It may feel like a fresh page rather than just a new address, but I would ask what new direction the person actually wants.
options.zh: 它可能像新階段而不只是新地址，但我會問當事人真正想展開甚麼方向。

options.en: I thought a change in postal details was enough to tell us that the person wanted different goals.
options.zh: 我原以為，郵寄資料改變，就足以告訴我們當事人想換目標。

options.en: I would describe it as a fresh start before hearing why the person chose to move.
options.zh: 我會先把它形容為新開始，之後才聽當事人為甚麼搬。

dialogue.explanationZh: 先了解本人意圖，不把住址變化直接代替生活意義。

speaking.en: The move could be a fresh page rather than just a new address, but I want to decide which plans to begin and which connections to keep.
speaking.zh: 搬遷可以是新階段，而不只是新地址，但我想自己決定開始哪些計劃、保留哪些連繫。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說新機會與延續的關係。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你搬進合住屋後，第一次邀家人來，由你安排飯菜而不是一直跟隨他們的計劃。你替家庭相簿寫圖說，想紀念自己開始作主人招待人的新角色，也保留舊家庭連繫，不說搬家抹去了過去。用一至兩句英文寫圖說。

examples.en: Hosting our first family meal made the move feel like a fresh page rather than just a new address. I was beginning to welcome people in my own way, while the familiar stories still belonged at the table.
examples.zh: 第一次招待家人吃飯，讓搬遷感覺是新階段，而不只是換地址。我開始用自己的方式迎接大家，熟悉的故事仍在餐桌上有位置。

examples.en: This meal marked a fresh page rather than just a new address: for once, I planned the welcome instead of following someone else’s arrangements. The old family connections were part of the beginning, not something I had left out.
examples.zh: 這頓飯標記了新階段，而不只是換地址：這次是我安排招待，而不是跟隨別人的計劃。舊家庭連繫是起點的一部分，不是被我丟下的東西。

writing.selfCheckZh: 以實際招待角色的轉變寫相簿圖說，交代新階段及延續；不只報地址，也不把新的自主等同過去沒有價值。

takeaways.en: The new placement gave her a fresh page rather than just a new address when it allowed her to return to the design work she had missed.
takeaways.zh: 新安排讓她重拾想念的設計工作，因此帶來新階段，而不只是換了地址。

takeaways.en: He hoped for a fresh page rather than just a new address, so he named the evening classes he wanted to make time for.
takeaways.zh: 他希望有新階段，而不只是換地址，所以說明自己想留時間參加哪些晚間課程。

lessons.titleEn: pull the rug out from under someone
lessons.titleZh: 突然抽走依靠，令人失去穩定

target.pattern: (?:\bpull(?:s|ed|ing)? the rug out from under (?:them|me|us|her|him|you|someone)\b)|(?:\b(?:pull|pulls|pulled|pulling) the rug out from under local people\b)

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Constant moves can pull the rug out from under them.
sources.expression: pull the rug out from under them

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 127, row 9; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: A policy should not pull the rug out from under local people.
sources.expression: pull the rug out from under local people

brief.meaningEn: Suddenly remove an expected source of support or security and leave someone destabilised.
brief.meaningZh: 突然抽走別人原本依靠的支持或保障，使對方失去穩定。
brief.grammar: pull the rug out from under someone, including local people; pulled is the past form. The lost 'rug' is expected support or security.
brief.boundaryZh: 要有突然失去依靠或保障的語境，不是任何調整都算；也不能單憑這個比喻判定對方蓄意傷害或此後一定失敗。
brief.misconceptionZh: 要有突然失去依靠或保障的語境，不是任何調整都算；也不能單憑這個比喻判定對方蓄意傷害或此後一定失敗。
brief.outcomeZh: 理解「突然抽走依靠，令人失去穩定」的語境及用法，並在新情境寫出自然句子。

listening.en: The workshop group had planned around a promised room, so cancelling it without warning pulled the rug out from under them just before rehearsals; they now had to find another place.
listening.zh: 工作坊小組按已答應提供的房間作安排，所以在排練前毫無預告地取消，突然抽走了他們的依靠；他們現在得另找地方。
listening.promptZh: 先只聽示範句。說話者想表達甚麼？

options.en: 原先答應的支持突然撤回，令小組的安排失去依靠。
房間從未答應提供，小組只是曾經問過。
小組早已知道取消安排，並已完成其他場地的排練。
說話者只是在說排練內容太難，沒有提場地承諾。

listening.explanationZh: promised room/without warning 說明突然抽走支持，現在仍要另找地方。

reply.promptEn: Why was the cancellation so disruptive?
reply.promptZh: 取消安排為甚麼造成這麼大影響？

options.en: It pulled the rug out from under them because they had built the rehearsal plan around a promised room.
options.zh: 它突然抽走他們的依靠，因為排練計劃是按已答應的房間安排。

options.en: They had relied on the room being available and had almost no warning to arrange an alternative.
options.zh: 他們一直依靠那房間可用，卻幾乎沒有預告時間另作安排。

options.en: The support they had planned around disappeared just before they needed it.
options.zh: 他們據以作計劃的支持，在需要用時前夕突然消失。

options.en: The problem was the unexpected withdrawal, not simply a preference for a different room.
options.zh: 問題在於突然撤回，不只是偏好另一房間。

reply.explanationZh: 四種回應都能回答這個問題；含有本課表達的回應另外獲得金句標記。

scene.promptZh: 場地方提前數周提出換房，兩個房間交接期間都可用，排練時間照舊，小組也表示有足夠安排空間。評論只因房號變了，就用這個比喻。哪句較謹慎？

options.en: A planned change with continuing support does not by itself show that the venue pulled the rug out from under them.
options.zh: 有計劃而支持持續的調整，本身不顯示場地方突然抽走了小組依靠。

options.en: The different room number establishes an unexpected loss of the support the group depended on.
options.zh: 房號不同，足以確立小組所依靠的支持突然失去。

options.en: Accepting an alternative means the group had never relied on the original arrangement.
options.zh: 接受替代安排，表示小組從未依靠原來安排。

scene.explanationZh: 需看突然性與支持是否撤走，不能只看有改動，也不能倒推原來沒有依靠。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種推論不宜由 pulled the rug out from under them 得出？

options.en: 有人突然失去原先依靠的支持。
撤回支持的人一定蓄意使對方失敗。
當事人可能需要重新安排，但結果仍未確定。

contrast.explanationZh: 這個比喻描述衝擊，不單獨證明動機或最終結果。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友認為小組既然還可另找地方，就不應說突然取消造成衝擊；你想區分能應變和原有支持被抽走。哪句最好？

options.en: They may find another room, but the sudden cancellation still pulled the rug out from under them at a crucial point.
options.zh: 他們可能找到另一房間，但突然取消仍在關鍵時候抽走了依靠。

options.en: I assumed having any possible alternative meant the original promise had not mattered to their plan.
options.zh: 我原以為，只要有任何替代可能，原來承諾就不影響計劃。

options.en: I would wait for the final venue to be found before recognising any disruption to the preparation.
options.zh: 我會等找到最終場地，才承認準備工作受到影響。

dialogue.explanationZh: 可重新找支持，不等於突然失去舊支持沒有影響；也不用先知最終結果才承認目前困難。

speaking.en: Withdrawing the agreed editing help without telling my partner pulled the rug out from under her when she was preparing the final version.
speaking.zh: 沒有告知合作伙伴就撤回議定的編輯協助，在她準備定稿時突然抽走了依靠。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再交代甚麼依靠被突然撤回。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：社團原獲答應暫存訪問資料箱，管理員現通知明天就要全取走。你已找到新存放空間，但那裏還未準備好；你想商量先取最急的一批、其餘多留三天，避免突然中斷既有依靠。用一至兩句英文提出過渡安排，不指控對方蓄意造成困難。

examples.en: Ending the agreed storage tomorrow would pull the rug out from under us before our new storage space is ready. Could we collect the urgent boxes first and agree three more days for the rest?
examples.zh: 新存放空間還未準備好，如果明天就結束議定的儲存安排，會突然抽走我們的依靠。我們可否先取急用箱子，其餘多留三天？

examples.en: The sudden end to the storage arrangement has pulled the rug out from under us, so I would like to agree a staged collection. We can take the urgent boxes tomorrow; could the remaining boxes stay for three days while we prepare the new storage space?
examples.zh: 儲存安排突然結束，抽走了我們的依靠，所以我想議定分批領取。我們明天可先取急用箱子；準備新存放空間期間，其餘可否多留三天？

writing.selfCheckZh: 指出突然失去依靠的具體困難，提出可協議過渡與自己可完成的一步；不把需要商量當已獲延長，也不由衝擊推定惡意。

takeaways.en: The unexpected loss of the agreed transport pulled the rug out from under us on the morning of the exhibition.
takeaways.zh: 展覽當日早上，議定的交通安排突然沒有了，抽走了我們的依靠。

takeaways.en: Closing the only evening clinic without notice would pull the rug out from under local people.
takeaways.zh: 若毫無預告便關閉唯一的夜間診所，會令區內居民突然失去重要支援。

lessons.titleZh: 輾轉短住，難以安頓日常

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: The family felt as if they were living out of a suitcase.

brief.meaningEn: Spend a period in temporary accommodation with belongings kept packed, often while moving between places, without settling into an ordinary home routine.
brief.meaningZh: 一段時間臨時住宿、行李仍未安頓，常伴隨輾轉住處，難以建立平常居家作息。
brief.grammar: live/lives/lived/living out of a suitcase; often a temporary travel or moving situation, not necessarily lack of an owned home. Repeated moves are common, but an unsettled temporary stay with belongings still packed can also fit.
brief.boundaryZh: 重點是臨時流動、難安頓的生活狀態，不是行李數量或是否有物業；一次旅程也不一定已構成長期狀態。
brief.misconceptionZh: 重點是臨時流動、難安頓的生活狀態，不是行李數量或是否有物業；一次旅程也不一定已構成長期狀態。
brief.outcomeZh: 理解「輾轉短住，難以安頓日常」的語境及用法，並在新情境寫出自然句子。

listening.en: After three borrowed rooms in one month, we felt as if we were living out of a suitcase; I kept the work notebook packed because I never knew where I would have space to use it next.
listening.zh: 一個月借住三個房間後，我們覺得像一直輾轉短住、無法安頓；我把工作筆記本留在行李裏，因為不知道下一處哪裏有空間使用。
listening.promptZh: 先只聽示範句。說話者想表達甚麼？

options.en: 頻繁換臨時住處，令普通工作日常難以安頓。
他們已固定住在同一房間多年，只偶爾整理筆記。
說話者確定下一處工作空間，已把筆記本放好不用再搬。
他們只是把工作改成全用電子筆記，沒有提住處變化。

listening.explanationZh: three rooms/month 及不知下一處空間，說明流動而未安頓，不是行李本身的大小。

reply.promptEn: What was difficult about that month?
reply.promptZh: 那個月有甚麼難處？

options.en: We were living out of a suitcase, moving between temporary rooms without an ordinary work routine.
options.zh: 我們輾轉短住，沒有安頓的工作日常。

options.en: Each temporary room meant finding somewhere different to set up the notebook again.
options.zh: 每個臨時房間，都要重新找不同位置放好筆記本。

options.en: I could not settle the small arrangements that usually make everyday work predictable.
options.zh: 我無法安頓那些平常令日常工作可預計的小安排。

options.en: The repeated moves kept interrupting our sense of having a regular base.
options.zh: 反覆搬動，不斷打斷我們有固定落腳處的感覺。

reply.explanationZh: 四種回應都能回答這個問題；含有本課表達的回應另外獲得金句標記。

scene.promptZh: 人物保留原有家，但三個月內不斷到外地工作、住短租房，每次剛建立作息又要走。朋友說有原有家就不能用這個表達。哪句最好？

options.en: Keeping a home elsewhere does not prevent her from living out of a suitcase during this unsettled period of work travel.
options.zh: 在別處保留家，不妨礙她這段流動出差期間仍是輾轉短住、難以安頓。

options.en: Owning or keeping a home elsewhere establishes that her present daily routine is already settled.
options.zh: 在別處擁有或保留家，足以確立目前日常已安頓。

options.en: Repeated temporary stays show only that she enjoys travel, not that her routines are interrupted.
options.zh: 反覆臨時住宿只顯示她喜歡旅遊，不表示日常被打斷。

scene.explanationZh: 看當前生活方式與作息，不用產權或假定享受旅遊來否認流動狀態。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種理解不宜由 living out of a suitcase 得出？

options.en: 當事人一段時間可能難以建立固定日常。
當事人在任何地方都不可能有自己的家。
可以描述有原有家卻長期輾轉出差的狀態。

contrast.explanationZh: 流動短住不單獨說明原有住處或產權。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說你明明還有家，就不應抱怨連續短住很難安頓；你想說明目前日常的實際情況。哪句最好？

options.en: I still have a home, but I have been living out of a suitcase between placements, with little chance to establish a routine.
options.zh: 我仍有家，但在各次安排之間一直輾轉短住，很少機會建立日常。

options.en: I assumed keeping the home meant I would have the same daily arrangements while staying elsewhere.
options.zh: 我原以為，保留原有家就表示住在別處時也會有相同日常安排。

options.en: I would describe the whole period only by whether the temporary rooms were pleasant.
options.zh: 我只會按臨時房間是否宜人，形容整段生活。

dialogue.explanationZh: 可同時有原有家和未安頓的目前生活；房間舒適與日常穩定也不是同一問題。

speaking.en: I have been living out of a suitcase between short assignments, so I would welcome a week in one place to organise an ordinary routine.
speaking.zh: 我在短期任務之間一直輾轉短住，所以很希望在同一地方留一周，整理平常作息。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說流動短住對日常有甚麼影響。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：義工組織問你能否再到另一城鎮支援兩周。你剛連續輾轉短住多周，這次想留在同一落腳處，也可遠端整理報名資料。用一至兩句英文婉拒這次移動任務，提出可做的另一種幫忙，不把決定說成以後永不外出。

examples.en: I have been living out of a suitcase for weeks, so I need to stay in one place this time. I cannot take the travelling role, but I could organise the registration records remotely.
examples.zh: 我已輾轉短住多周，所以這次需要留在同一地方。我不能接下需要外出的角色，但可遠端整理報名資料。

examples.en: After weeks of living out of a suitcase, I would like a more settled base for the next fortnight. Could I help with the registration records from here instead of joining this trip?
examples.zh: 輾轉短住多周後，我希望接下來兩周有較安定的落腳處。我可否留在這裏協助整理報名資料，而不是參加這次外出？

writing.selfCheckZh: 交代當前短住流動的需要，清楚婉拒這次任務並提出可行替代；不否定過往參與，也不把短期決定說成終身承諾。

takeaways.en: They were living out of a suitcase between festival jobs, finding a different kitchen and bus route every few days.
takeaways.zh: 他們在各次藝術節工作之間輾轉短住，每隔幾天就要找不同廚房和巴士路線。

takeaways.en: She had lived out of a suitcase during the recording tour and was glad to leave her notes on one desk again.
takeaways.zh: 錄音巡迴期間她一直輾轉短住，所以很高興終於能再把筆記放在同一張桌上。

lessons.titleZh: 原有興奮逐漸減退

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: After five moves, the excitement can wear thin.

brief.meaningEn: Become gradually weaker or less convincing, enjoyable or effective through repetition or continued demands.
brief.meaningZh: 隨重複或持續消耗而逐漸減弱；這裏指原有興奮慢慢消退。
brief.grammar: the excitement can wear thin; wore thin / has worn thin; a feeling, explanation or patience may wear thin, with the subject specifying what weakens.
brief.boundaryZh: 是感受或效力漸弱，不等於從來沒有喜歡，也不自動表示事情必須停止；需看實際感受與選擇。
brief.misconceptionZh: 是感受或效力漸弱，不等於從來沒有喜歡，也不自動表示事情必須停止；需看實際感受與選擇。
brief.outcomeZh: 理解「原有興奮逐漸減退」的語境及用法，並在新情境寫出自然句子。
brief.sourceClassificationNote: The figurative predicate wear thin is taught through fading excitement, not as a separate dictionary sense for each feeling or subject.

listening.en: The first month of the touring job felt exciting, but the excitement began to wear thin as each evening became another hurried check-in, and I missed having time to talk to people.
listening.zh: 巡迴工作的第一個月令人興奮，但每晚都變成匆忙入住，原有興奮便開始減退，我也想念有時間跟人談話的日子。
listening.promptZh: 先只聽示範句。說話者想表達甚麼？

options.en: 起初確有興奮，重複的匆忙生活後感受開始減弱。
說話者從未對工作感到興奮，只是假裝喜歡。
說話者已正式辭職，這裏主要在報告離職程序。
每晚匆忙入住，令說話者比初時更興奮。

listening.explanationZh: first month exciting/began 表明前後轉變；沒有說從未喜歡或已作最後去留決定。

reply.promptEn: How did your feelings about the touring job change?
reply.promptZh: 你對巡迴工作的感受有甚麼改變？

options.en: The excitement began to wear thin when the evenings became a repeated rush between places.
options.zh: 晚上變成反覆奔波後，原有興奮開始減退。

options.en: I enjoyed the first month, but later wanted more ordinary time with people.
options.zh: 我喜歡第一個月，但後來想有更多跟人平常相處的時間。

options.en: The novelty mattered less as the hurried routine became more noticeable.
options.zh: 當匆忙習慣變得更明顯，新鮮感的重要性便下降。

options.en: I was still doing the job, but no longer felt the same enthusiasm about the travel.
options.zh: 我仍在做這份工作，但對外出不再有原來的熱情。

reply.explanationZh: 四種回應都能回答這個問題；含有本課表達的回應另外獲得金句標記。

scene.promptZh: 一個反覆使用的活動宣傳理由，最初讓會員期待，幾個月後卻愈來愈難令他們信服；活動尚未決定取消。哪句最準確？

options.en: The explanation is starting to wear thin, though the decision about the activity is still open.
options.zh: 這個解釋開始失去說服力，但活動的去留仍未決定。

options.en: The activity has already been cancelled because nobody ever accepted the explanation.
options.zh: 活動已取消，因為從來沒有人接受過那個解釋。

options.en: Repeating the explanation shows that members find it more convincing each time.
options.zh: 重複解釋，顯示會員每次都覺得更有說服力。

scene.explanationZh: 最初有效而後漸弱，跟從未有效或最後已取消不同。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種推論不宜由 the excitement is wearing thin 得出？

options.en: 原有熱情可能已不如從前。
當事人從來沒有真心期待過這件事。
仍可另外討論是否繼續及怎樣調整。

contrast.explanationZh: 漸弱承認有前後變化，不否定早期感受。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說你既然現在沒那麼期待巡演，以前的喜歡一定是假的；你想說清感受會變。哪句最好？

options.en: The excitement can wear thin without the earlier enjoyment being false; I liked the novelty, but now notice the cost of the rushed routine.
options.zh: 興奮可以逐漸減退，而不表示以前的享受是假的；我喜歡過新鮮感，但現在更留意匆忙日常的代價。

options.en: I assumed a genuine interest would feel exactly the same after months of repetition.
options.zh: 我原以為，真正的興趣在幾個月重複後，感覺仍會完全一樣。

options.en: I would describe my first month only by how tired I feel about the routine now.
options.zh: 我只會按現在對日常有多疲倦，形容第一個月。

dialogue.explanationZh: 分清早期真實享受與後來減退，不能用目前感受改寫以前。

speaking.en: The novelty has worn thin, but I would like to discuss a different schedule before deciding whether to leave the project.
speaking.zh: 新鮮感已減退，但在決定是否離開項目前，我想先討論不同的時間安排。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再分清熱情減退與最後去留決定。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你要回覆訂閱盒公司的續訂邀請。每月拆盒最初有趣，但近來很多內容重複，你不想只因早期喜歡便自動續訂，想先問下季內容有何不同。用一至兩句英文交代感受與問題。

examples.en: The excitement of opening the box has worn thin as the contents have become repetitive. Before I renew, could you tell me what will be different in the next season?
examples.zh: 隨着內容變得重複，拆盒的興奮已減退。續訂前，你可否告訴我下季會有甚麼不同？

examples.en: I enjoyed the early boxes, but the novelty is starting to wear thin. Could you explain the changes planned for the next season so I can decide whether the subscription still suits me?
examples.zh: 我喜歡過初期的盒子，但新鮮感開始減退。你可否解釋下季計劃有甚麼改變，讓我決定訂閱是否仍適合自己？

writing.selfCheckZh: 承認最初享受與目前減退，提出決定前想了解的具體資訊；不把變化寫成從來沒有喜歡，亦不預先聲稱對方一定能恢復興趣。

takeaways.en: The joke wore thin after the host repeated it between every performance, and the audience became less responsive.
takeaways.zh: 主持在每場表演之間都重複那個笑話後，它失去了趣味，觀眾反應也變淡了。

takeaways.en: Her patience was wearing thin after several unanswered messages about the missing equipment.
takeaways.zh: 她為遺失器材發了多則訊息都未獲回覆，耐性正逐漸耗盡。

lessons.titleZh: 開始在一個地方安定生活

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: They are thinking about putting down roots.

brief.meaningEn: Begin to settle in a place and build a stable life or continuing connections there.
brief.meaningZh: 開始在一個地方安頓，建立較穩定的生活或持續連繫。
brief.grammar: put down roots in a town/community; putting down roots; put is also the past form. Related build deep roots emphasises the depth of ties developed over time.
brief.boundaryZh: 安頓可以逐步形成，不要求買屋、生於當地或保證一生不走；也不是短暫停留本身就已扎根。
brief.misconceptionZh: 安頓可以逐步形成，不要求買屋、生於當地或保證一生不走；也不是短暫停留本身就已扎根。
brief.outcomeZh: 理解「開始在一個地方安定生活」的語境及用法，並在新情境寫出自然句子。

listening.en: After several temporary placements, the couple wanted to put down roots in the town, joining ordinary weekly activities and making plans that did not depend on leaving again next month.
listening.zh: 幾次臨時安排後，這對伴侶想在鎮上安定下來，參加平常每周活動，訂立不以次月再離開為前提的計劃。
listening.promptZh: 先只聽示範句。說話者想表達甚麼？

options.en: 他們想從反覆短住轉向較穩定的生活與連繫。
他們只打算留一晚，沒有考慮之後生活。
他們認為要先在當地出生，才有資格參與。
他們已承諾終身不搬走，才開始每周活動。

listening.explanationZh: temporary placements 對比 continuing weekly plans；不是生地、產權或永不離開的條件。

reply.promptEn: What do they want after the temporary placements?
reply.promptZh: 幾次臨時安排後，他們想要甚麼？

options.en: They want to put down roots and begin building a stable life in the town.
options.zh: 他們想在鎮上扎根，開始建立穩定生活。

options.en: They would like ordinary weekly connections instead of planning around another immediate move.
options.zh: 他們想有平常每周的連繫，不再圍繞下一次即將搬動作安排。

options.en: Their next plans are about staying involved locally for a while.
options.zh: 他們下一步的計劃，是在當地持續參與一段時間。

options.en: They hope to become part of the town’s everyday life rather than treat it only as a temporary stop.
options.zh: 他們希望成為鎮上日常生活的一部分，不只把它當臨時停靠處。

reply.explanationZh: 四種回應都能回答這個問題；含有本課表達的回應另外獲得金句標記。

scene.promptZh: 人物到一城鎮出差兩晚，明說只需睡覺休息、之後回原有生活，沒有長期參與打算。朋友想用 put down roots 介紹這趟行程。哪句最好？

options.en: A two-night work stop alone does not show a plan to put down roots there.
options.zh: 單是兩晚工作停留，不顯示有在當地安頓的計劃。

options.en: Any stay in the town establishes a decision to build a continuing life there.
options.zh: 只要在鎮上住過，就確立了建立持續生活的決定。

options.en: The visitor has described seeking a continuing local role rather than returning to the existing life after the work stop.
options.zh: 訪客已描述想找持續的本地角色，而不是工作短停後回原有生活。

scene.explanationZh: 目前只給短暫工作停留和返回原生活的打算，沒有持續參與線索；不能把任何住宿都當扎根。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種理解不宜由 put down roots 得出？

options.en: 開始跟地方建立較持續的生活安排。
必須先擁有當地物業，才可以安頓。
可逐步參加當地的日常活動。

contrast.explanationZh: 扎根是生活連繫的圖像，不以物業產權作必要條件。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說你租住而不是買屋，就不算想安頓；你想談實際生活計劃。哪句最好？

options.en: I can put down roots through continuing relationships and ordinary routines; owning the building is a separate question.
options.zh: 我可以透過持續關係和平常作息安頓；是否擁有那幢樓是另一問題。

options.en: I assumed the housing ownership label told us whether someone wanted continuing local connections.
options.zh: 我原以為，房屋的擁有權類別，就能告訴我們一個人是否想持續在當地連繫。

options.en: I would wait to discuss community activities until I knew whether I would ever buy the flat.
options.zh: 我會等知道自己將來會否買那單位，才討論社區活動。

dialogue.explanationZh: 把安頓的生活意義與產權分開，不要由租住直接否定參與。

speaking.en: We are thinking about putting down roots here, so we would like to know which local activities we could join regularly.
speaking.zh: 我們正考慮在這裏安頓，所以想知道有哪些本地活動可以固定參加。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再以持續參與說明安頓的打算。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：社區花園請你決定接不接一塊需要整季照料的地。你想在這區安定生活，但還未清楚值班安排，也不想只因熱情便承諾做不到的事。用一至兩句英文表達意願，並問清每周照料的要求。

examples.en: I would like to put down roots in this neighbourhood, and the garden could be part of that. Before I commit to a plot, could you explain the weekly care and the arrangements when someone is away?
examples.zh: 我想在這個社區安頓，花園可成為其中一部分。在承諾接一塊地之前，你可否解釋每周照料，以及有人離開時的安排？

examples.en: We are hoping to put down roots here, so we are interested in caring for a plot through the season. Could we discuss the rota first to make sure we can offer the regular help it needs?
examples.zh: 我們希望在這裏安頓，所以有興趣整季照料一塊地。我們可否先談值班表，確保自己能提供所需的固定幫忙？

writing.selfCheckZh: 以較持續參與表達安頓意願，也問清實際責任再承諾；不把一句意願當成已建立深厚關係，也不把安頓等同一定買屋。

takeaways.en: She began to put down roots by joining the weekly repair group and getting to know the people on her street.
takeaways.zh: 她參加每周維修小組、認識同街的人，開始在當地安頓。

takeaways.en: They were putting down roots in the village, but still wanted to visit the friends they had left in the city.
takeaways.zh: 他們正在村裏安頓，但仍想探望留在城市的朋友。

lessons.titleEn: at the mercy of rent increases
lessons.titleZh: 受租金上調左右，缺乏控制

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Tenants may feel at the mercy of rent increases.
sources.expression: at the mercy of rent increases

brief.meaningEn: Vulnerable to rent rises whose timing or size one cannot adequately control.
brief.meaningZh: 容易受到自己難以充分控制的租金上調影響。
brief.grammar: be/feel/leave someone at the mercy of rent increases; at the mercy of names exposure to an outside force, not proof that no response is possible.
brief.boundaryZh: 表達缺乏控制的感受或處境，不單獨確立租約條款、法律權利或業主動機；也不是說當事人完全沒有任何可做的事。
brief.misconceptionZh: 表達缺乏控制的感受或處境，不單獨確立租約條款、法律權利或業主動機；也不是說當事人完全沒有任何可做的事。
brief.outcomeZh: 理解「受租金上調左右，缺乏控制」的語境及用法，並在新情境寫出自然句子。

listening.en: In the story, Maya felt at the mercy of rent increases because she could not predict what the next renewal would cost; she wanted clearer information before choosing how long to stay.
listening.zh: 故事裏，Maya 因無法預計下次續租費用，覺得受租金上調左右；她想先有更清楚資訊，再選擇住多久。
listening.promptZh: 先只聽示範句。說話者想表達甚麼？

options.en: 她對難以預計的外在費用缺乏控制，想先了解資訊。
她已收到下次續租確切金額，現在只是比較付款日期。
她已決定離開，並已完成下一份租約。
她確定每次加租的動機都是針對自己。

listening.explanationZh: could not predict 說明缺乏控制，wanted information 說明仍可採取下一步；沒有確認條款或動機。

reply.promptEn: Why did Maya want clearer information before deciding how long to stay?
reply.promptZh: Maya 為甚麼想先有清楚資訊，才決定住多久？

options.en: She felt at the mercy of rent increases because she could not predict the renewal cost.
options.zh: 她無法預計續租費用，所以覺得受租金上調左右。

options.en: The uncertainty made it difficult to plan her next period there.
options.zh: 不確定性令她難以計劃接下來住在那裏的一段時間。

options.en: She wanted to understand an outside cost that could affect her plans.
options.zh: 她想了解可能影響計劃的外在費用。

options.en: She did not yet have the information she needed to compare the available arrangements.
options.zh: 她尚未有比較現有安排所需的資訊。

reply.explanationZh: 四種回應都能回答這個問題；含有本課表達的回應另外獲得金句標記。

scene.promptZh: 虛構故事明說人物這一年的租金已確定，不會上調；她擔心的是通勤時間。旁白想用本課表達解釋她目前的擔憂。哪句較準確？

options.en: The stated concern is travel time, so this account does not establish that she is at the mercy of rent increases this year.
options.zh: 已說明的擔憂是通勤時間，所以這份敘述沒有確立她今年受租金上調左右。

options.en: Worry about the journey establishes that an unpredictable rent rise is the immediate problem.
options.zh: 擔心路程，足以確立眼前問題是無法預計的加租。

options.en: A fixed rent for this year tells us that every other part of her housing situation is secure.
options.zh: 今年租金固定，就能告訴我們其他住屋情況也全部穩妥。

scene.explanationZh: 按已給的費用與擔憂判斷，不把另一種不確定性當成加租，也不把單一固定費用擴大成所有保障。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種推論不宜只由 feel at the mercy of rent increases 得出？

options.en: 人物感到自己的計劃易受外在費用影響。
已能確立業主的法律權限及每次加租是否合法。
仍需了解實際安排，才能知道有哪些選擇。

contrast.explanationZh: 感受或比喻不代替條款及具體權利資訊。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說 Maya 既然可詢問續租資料，就不會有受外力左右的感覺；你想區分能問與能控制。哪句最好？

options.en: She can ask for information and still feel at the mercy of rent increases; asking does not mean she controls the next figure.
options.zh: 她可以詢問資料，也仍覺得受租金上調左右；能問不表示能控制下次金額。

options.en: I assumed that receiving the next figure would make later renewals predictable as well.
options.zh: 我原以為，收到下一次金額，就表示之後續租也都可預計。

options.en: I would treat her worry as a confirmed account of the landlord’s intentions.
options.zh: 我會把她的擔心，當成已確認的業主意圖。

dialogue.explanationZh: 詢問可了解一項擬議安排，不等於能控制金額或之後所有續租；也不能從擔心確認動機。

speaking.en: They felt at the mercy of rent increases, so their first request was for clear information about the proposed renewal.
speaking.zh: 他們覺得受租金上調左右，所以首先要求清楚交代擬議的續租安排。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再把缺乏控制的感受與可提出的要求分開。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你編輯一篇人物訪問。受訪者說自己「覺得受加租左右」，草稿卻刪了「覺得」，寫成所有租戶都完全沒選擇。你想請作者恢復這是個人感受的範圍，並保留受訪者實際採取的查詢。用一至兩句英文提出修改。

examples.en: Please keep ‘she felt at the mercy of rent increases’ as her own description, rather than turn it into a statement that every tenant has no choices. The paragraph should also retain the questions she asked about the proposal.
examples.zh: 請保留「她覺得受租金上調左右」作她自己的描述，不把它改成每個租戶都沒有選擇的陳述。這段也應保留她就建議實際提出的問題。

examples.en: Could we restore the words ‘felt at the mercy of rent increases’ in the quotation and keep the account of her enquiries? That would preserve her perspective without making the broader claim added by the draft.
examples.zh: 我們可否在引文恢復「覺得受租金上調左右」，也保留她實際查詢的敘述？這樣能保存她的觀點，不加入草稿擴大的斷言。

writing.selfCheckZh: 提出具體引文與敘述修改，保存個人感受及實際行動；不把感到缺乏控制擴成所有人的事實，也不為求正面而刪掉不安。

takeaways.en: The tenants in the play felt at the mercy of rent increases when no one could tell them what the next agreement would cost.
takeaways.zh: 劇中租戶無人能告知下一份協議費用時，覺得受租金上調左右。

takeaways.en: Her character describes feeling at the mercy of rent increases while waiting for the renewal proposal, rather than claiming she already knows its terms.
takeaways.zh: 她的角色形容等待續租建議時，感到受租金上調左右，而不是聲稱已知道條款。

lessons.titleEn: money disappearing into someone else’s pocket
lessons.titleZh: 覺得錢流進別人口袋

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Rent can feel like money disappearing into someone else's pocket.

brief.meaningEn: A critical image of paying money away to someone else, especially while feeling one gains no lasting asset from it.
brief.meaningZh: 帶批評意味地形容錢付給別人，尤其當事人覺得自己沒有累積持久資產時。
brief.grammar: feel like money disappearing into someone else’s pocket; frame the perception with feel/seem rather than present the image as a complete cost assessment.
brief.boundaryZh: 描述付錢者的感受，不是證明付款毫無用途、收款者不誠實，或某種住屋選擇一定較佳；租金也可能支付實際住宿服務。
brief.misconceptionZh: 描述付錢者的感受，不是證明付款毫無用途、收款者不誠實，或某種住屋選擇一定較佳；租金也可能支付實際住宿服務。
brief.outcomeZh: 理解「覺得錢流進別人口袋」的語境及用法，並在新情境寫出自然句子。

listening.en: To the character, each rent payment felt like money disappearing into someone else’s pocket because she was not building an asset, though she acknowledged that it paid for the place she was living in.
listening.zh: 對那個角色而言，每次交租都像錢流進別人口袋，因為她沒有累積資產，雖然她承認租金支付了自己正在住的地方。
listening.promptZh: 先只聽示範句。說話者想表達甚麼？

options.en: 她對未累積資產感到不滿，同時承認租金提供住處。
她已證明房東收款涉及不誠實行為。
她認為自己付了款，卻從未獲提供任何住處。
她正在列出各種選擇的完整成本，已得出適合所有人的結論。

listening.explanationZh: felt like/because 說主觀評價，though 承認住宿用途，不是欺詐或所有選擇的完整判定。

reply.promptEn: Why did the rent payment frustrate the character?
reply.promptZh: 交租為甚麼令那個角色不滿？

options.en: It felt like money disappearing into someone else’s pocket because she was not building an asset of her own.
options.zh: 因為沒有累積自己的資產，她覺得錢像流進別人口袋。

options.en: She disliked paying a regular amount without gaining ownership.
options.zh: 她不喜歡固定付款，卻沒有取得擁有權。

options.en: The payment gave her somewhere to live, but not the lasting asset she wanted.
options.zh: 付款給她住處，卻不是她想要的持久資產。

options.en: Her frustration concerned what she was not accumulating, rather than a claim that she had received no accommodation.
options.zh: 她不滿的是沒有累積的東西，而不是聲稱沒有獲得住宿。

reply.explanationZh: 四種回應都能回答這個問題；含有本課表達的回應另外獲得金句標記。

scene.promptZh: 劇團成員不滿演出服租一周後要歸還，說費用像錢流進別人口袋；但她已穿着完成演出，店方也按約提供了服裝。宣傳稿想因此指控店方沒有交付服務。哪句最準確？

options.en: Describing the fee as “money disappearing into someone else’s pocket” expresses her frustration about not keeping the costume, not proof that the agreed use was never provided.
options.zh: 把租金形容為錢流進別人口袋，表達她對不能留下服裝的不滿，不是證明沒有提供議定使用。

options.en: Her frustration establishes that the shop withheld the costume throughout the agreed rental week.
options.zh: 她的不滿，足以確立店方在議定租用周內一直沒有交出服裝。

options.en: Using the costume establishes that she was content with returning it and had no concern about ownership.
options.zh: 使用過服裝，足以確立她樂意歸還，對擁有權沒有任何不滿。

scene.explanationZh: 實際使用與沒有留下物件可同時存在；不滿不是未交付證據，收到服務也不證明對所有條件滿意。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種推論不宜由 money disappearing into someone else’s pocket 得出？

options.en: 說話者可能對金錢流出感到不滿。
這個圖像已完整證明另一種住屋安排在她今年的總成本較低。
仍要分清感受、實際服務與個人需要。

contrast.explanationZh: 一個批評圖像沒有包含完整成本和不同人的需要。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友以這個圖像說任何人都不應租住；你想承認感受，也保留具體情況。哪句最好？

options.en: I understand why rent can feel like money disappearing into someone else’s pocket, but that feeling alone does not compare the options for each person.
options.zh: 我明白為甚麼租金會像錢流進別人口袋，但單憑這種感受，沒有比較每個人的選項。

options.en: I thought not gaining ownership meant the payment had supplied no useful accommodation.
options.zh: 我原以為，沒有取得擁有權，就表示付款沒有提供有用住宿。

options.en: I would use that image as the whole comparison before asking what the person needs.
options.zh: 我會先把那個圖像當成完整比較，之後才問當事人需要甚麼。

dialogue.explanationZh: 承認比喻的情緒而不讓它替代所有資訊；沒有擁有權不等於沒有住宿服務。

speaking.en: The payment felt like money disappearing into someone else’s pocket to him, but that was his frustration, not a full comparison of the available arrangements.
speaking.zh: 對他而言，付款像錢流進別人口袋，但那是他的不滿，不是對現有安排的完整比較。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再把人物感受與完整比較分開。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：朋友用「交租只是把錢送進別人口袋」否定你短期租住的選擇。你理解沒有累積物業資產的感受，但目前想保留外地交流的可能，也重視已有住宿安排。用一至兩句英文回覆，說明你的需要，不替所有人作住屋決定。

examples.en: I understand why rent may feel like money disappearing into someone else’s pocket, but I am also paying for somewhere to live while keeping the exchange opportunity open. I want to compare the arrangements against my present needs, not decide from that image alone.
examples.zh: 我明白為甚麼租金會像錢流進別人口袋，但我也在支付實際住處，同時保留外地交流機會。我想按目前需要比較安排，而不是只憑那個圖像決定。

examples.en: Money disappearing into someone else’s pocket captures one frustration about renting, but it does not describe everything I need this year. A place to stay and flexibility for the exchange both matter to my decision.
examples.zh: 錢流進別人口袋，道出一種對租住的不滿，但沒有概括我今年的全部需要。可住的地方，以及參加交流的彈性，都影響我的決定。

writing.selfCheckZh: 承認批評圖像表達的感受，再以自己的實際需要作回應；不把沒有物業資產等同沒有服務，也不聲稱某種選擇必定適合每個人。

takeaways.en: In his letter, the annual fee felt like money disappearing into someone else’s pocket when he thought only about ownership, not the shared studio access it provided.
takeaways.zh: 他在信中只想到擁有權、沒想到費用提供共用工作室的使用機會時，覺得年費像錢流進別人口袋。

takeaways.en: She used money disappearing into someone else’s pocket to describe her frustration with the payments, then listed the services they actually covered.
takeaways.zh: 她用錢流進別人口袋形容對付款的不滿，然後列出款項實際涵蓋的服務。

lessons.titleZh: 保留輕身轉換的自由

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Renting can help keep your feet light.

brief.meaningEn: Preserve the freedom to move or change plans without taking on commitments that make movement difficult.
brief.meaningZh: 保留移動或調整計劃的自由，避免承擔令轉換變得困難的牽絆。
brief.grammar: keep your feet light; the source uses a creative light-feet image for mobility, not a fixed instruction about how to walk.
brief.boundaryZh: 要說清保留哪種轉換空間；輕身不等於不負責任、完全不承諾，或每次轉換都沒有成本。
brief.misconceptionZh: 要說清保留哪種轉換空間；輕身不等於不負責任、完全不承諾，或每次轉換都沒有成本。
brief.outcomeZh: 理解「保留輕身轉換的自由」的語境及用法，並在新情境寫出自然句子。
brief.sourceClassificationNote: A contextual creative metaphor for flexibility, not an established whole-phrase dictionary idiom.

listening.en: The short placement let me keep my feet light while I learned which kind of archive work suited me; I still had agreed hours to complete before deciding where to apply next.
listening.zh: 短期安排讓我保留轉換自由，同時了解哪類檔案工作適合自己；在決定下一處申請前，我仍有議定工時要完成。
listening.promptZh: 先只聽示範句。說話者想表達甚麼？

options.en: 說話者保留下一步選擇，但仍需完成現有責任。
她把短期安排當成不用履行任何已答應工時。
她已決定終身留在同一職位，不再了解其他工作。
她的下一處申請已獲批，現有安排已結束。

listening.explanationZh: while learned 說探索中的彈性，still agreed hours 保留當前責任。

reply.promptEn: What did the short placement allow you to do?
reply.promptZh: 短期安排讓你做到甚麼？

options.en: It let me keep my feet light while finding out which archive work suited me.
options.zh: 它讓我在了解哪類檔案工作適合自己時，保留轉換自由。

options.en: I could learn about the work before making a longer commitment.
options.zh: 我可以先了解工作，再作較長承諾。

options.en: I had room to consider the next application while completing the agreed hours.
options.zh: 我可以在完成議定工時的同時，考慮下一次申請。

options.en: The arrangement preserved some choice without removing my present responsibilities.
options.zh: 安排保留了一些選擇，但沒有取消目前責任。

reply.explanationZh: 四種回應都能回答這個問題；含有本課表達的回應另外獲得金句標記。

scene.promptZh: 人物稱自己保留彈性，但她已答應全年每周到固定地點，現在才發現與外地課程重疊；她想只因角色名稱有「臨時」便說沒有牽絆。哪句最準確？

options.en: The temporary label does not by itself help her keep her feet light if the agreed dates still create a year-long conflict.
options.zh: 如果議定日期仍造成全年衝突，「臨時」名稱本身沒有幫她保留轉換自由。

options.en: Calling the role temporary means the agreed weekly dates no longer need to be discussed.
options.zh: 把角色稱為臨時，表示不必再討論已議定的每周日期。

options.en: Considering the course means she has already told the group which dates she cannot attend.
options.zh: 考慮那個課程，表示她已告訴小組哪些日期不能到。

scene.explanationZh: 看實際承諾而非角色名稱；發現衝突或考慮課程，不等於已完成溝通。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種理解不宜由 keep your feet light 的彈性語境得出？

options.en: 保留下一步調整空間。
已答應的責任可不告知別人便擱下。
短承諾也可能有需要完成的安排。

contrast.explanationZh: 輕身形容轉換空間，不提供不履約或不溝通的理由。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說你想保留下一步選擇，就應先答應所有新邀請再算；你想選擇較清楚的承諾。哪句最好？

options.en: I want to keep my feet light, so I would check the dates and responsibilities before accepting another role.
options.zh: 我想保留轉換自由，所以會先核對日期和責任，再接另一角色。

options.en: I thought flexibility meant leaving the dates unclear until both groups had planned around me.
options.zh: 我原以為，彈性就是等兩組都按我會參與來安排後，日期仍不說清。

options.en: I would compare only how interesting the invitations sound, not whether the commitments fit.
options.zh: 我只會比較邀請聽來多有趣，不看承諾能否配合。

dialogue.explanationZh: 清楚知道承諾範圍才有實際彈性，不把模糊或重疊當自由。

speaking.en: I would like to keep my feet light for the next few months, so I am choosing a short project with a clear finish and handover.
speaking.zh: 接下來幾個月，我想保留轉換自由，所以正選有清楚完結和交接的短項目。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再把保留彈性與清楚責任連起來。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：親人想送你一張需固定在房內的大工作桌，但你之後半年可能在不同地方短住。你感謝好意，想選能帶走的工具箱、到各處用共用桌，不想讓家具決定行程。用一至兩句英文解釋你的禮物偏好。

examples.en: Thank you for the generous offer, but I want to keep my feet light while my next base is uncertain. A portable tool case would help more than a fixed worktable, because I could use it at shared desks in different places.
examples.zh: 謝謝你慷慨提議，但下一個落腳處未定，我想保留輕身轉換的自由。便攜工具箱會比固定工作桌更有幫助，因為我可在不同地方的共用桌使用。

examples.en: I would like to keep my feet light for the coming months rather than plan my moves around a large table. Could we choose a tool case I can carry instead, while I use the shared workspaces available along the way?
examples.zh: 接下來幾個月，我想保留輕身轉換的自由，而不是圍繞大桌子安排搬動。我們可否改選能帶走的工具箱，讓我沿途使用可用的共用工作空間？

writing.selfCheckZh: 感謝心意，以具體物品及使用方式說明移動彈性；不只是聲稱要自由，也不把拒絕一種禮物寫成拒絕所有幫忙。

takeaways.en: A three-week exhibition project helped her keep her feet light while she waited to learn where the next course would take place.
takeaways.zh: 等待得知下一課程在哪裏舉行時，三周的展覽項目幫她保留了轉換自由。

takeaways.en: They wanted to keep their feet light, so they agreed a short trial and a review date before considering a longer partnership.
takeaways.zh: 他們想保留轉換自由，所以先議定短期試做及檢討日期，再考慮較長合作。

lessons.titleEn: not have all your eggs in one basket
lessons.titleZh: 不把全部希望放在單一選項

target.pattern: (?:\b(?:have|has|had|having|put(?:ting)?) all (?:my|our|their|your|her|his|the) eggs in one basket\b)|(?:\b(?:have|has|had|having|put(?:ting)?) all its eggs in one basket\b)

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Renting can help them not have all their eggs in one basket.
sources.expression: not have all their eggs in one basket

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 125, row 8; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: A supplier should not put all its eggs in one basket.
sources.expression: all its eggs in one basket

brief.meaningEn: Depend entirely on a single plan or source; the negative form recommends avoiding that concentration of dependence.
brief.meaningZh: 把希望或依靠全部集中在一個計劃或來源；否定式表示避免只依賴一個。
brief.grammar: have/put all your, their or its eggs in one basket; its can refer to a firm or supplier. The idiom concerns dependence on one option, not actual eggs.
brief.boundaryZh: 分散依靠不是保證成功，也不等於不認真投入任何一項；需有實際不同的選項，不只是同一來源換名稱。
brief.misconceptionZh: 分散依靠不是保證成功，也不等於不認真投入任何一項；需有實際不同的選項，不只是同一來源換名稱。
brief.outcomeZh: 理解「不把全部希望放在單一選項」的語境及用法，並在新情境寫出自然句子。

listening.en: We did not want to have all our eggs in one basket, so alongside the main interview request we asked a different archive about written accounts; either source might still say no.
listening.zh: 我們不想只依賴一個來源，所以除了主要訪問邀請，也向另一檔案館詢問書面敘述；任何一方仍可能拒絕。
listening.promptZh: 先只聽示範句。說話者想表達甚麼？

options.en: 小組找不同資料來源，減少只靠一個邀請的依賴，但未保證獲回覆。
小組已取得兩邊同意，現在只在安排印刷。
小組把同一封未回覆邀請改了標題，沒有接觸其他來源。
小組決定不再認真準備主要訪問，因為有另一封查詢。

listening.explanationZh: alongside/different archive 是另有來源，might say no 保留不確定；分散不等於放棄準備。

reply.promptEn: Why did the group contact a different archive too?
reply.promptZh: 小組為甚麼也聯絡另一檔案館？

options.en: They did not want to have all their eggs in one basket by relying on a single interview request.
options.zh: 他們不想只依賴一個訪問邀請，把全部希望集中在一處。

options.en: They wanted another possible route to information if the main request was declined.
options.zh: 如果主要邀請被拒，他們想有另一條可能的資料途徑。

options.en: A separate archive could reduce their dependence on one person’s availability.
options.zh: 另一檔案館可減少只依賴一個人的時間安排。

options.en: They were looking for an additional source without assuming either would agree.
options.zh: 他們正找額外來源，但沒有假定任何一方一定同意。

reply.explanationZh: 四種回應都能回答這個問題；含有本課表達的回應另外獲得金句標記。

scene.promptZh: 小組說自己已分散依靠，實際上所有三個計劃都要同一位尚未答應的受訪者先同意；只是成果格式不同。哪句最準確？

options.en: Different formats do not remove the fact that they have all their eggs in one basket if every plan depends on the same unconfirmed interview.
options.zh: 如果每個計劃都依賴同一未確認訪問，不同成果格式也沒有消除單一依靠。

options.en: Three formats establish three independent sources of agreement.
options.zh: 三種格式足以確立三個獨立的同意來源。

options.en: Depending on one interview means the interview is already certain to be refused.
options.zh: 依賴一個訪問，表示那個訪問已肯定會被拒。

scene.explanationZh: 看實際依賴是否同一關鍵條件，不以格式數量代來源，也不由風險推成已知失敗。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種理解不宜由 not have all your eggs in one basket 得出？

options.en: 不要只依賴單一計劃或來源。
只要有多個可能途徑，便無需認真準備其中任何一個。
另有途徑也仍可能有不確定性。

contrast.explanationZh: 分散依靠不取消各項準備，也不保證結果。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說查詢兩處資料就不用準備主要訪問；你想說明分散依靠與投入準備可並存。哪句最好？

options.en: We should not have all our eggs in one basket, but we should still prepare the main interview properly while the other request is pending.
options.zh: 我們不應只依賴單一來源，但另一查詢未有結果時，仍應好好準備主要訪問。

options.en: I thought another unanswered request meant we no longer needed questions for the main interview.
options.zh: 我原以為，另有一封未回覆查詢，就表示主要訪問不用備問題。

options.en: I would count the two requests as two confirmed sources before either has replied.
options.zh: 我會在任何一方回覆前，就把兩封查詢當成兩個已確認來源。

dialogue.explanationZh: 另有可能性不是已確認結果，也不是擱下主要工作。

speaking.en: We do not want to have all our eggs in one basket, so we will prepare another route while continuing to work carefully on the first plan.
speaking.zh: 我們不想只依賴單一選項，所以會準備另一途徑，同時繼續認真做好第一個計劃。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說明分散依靠而不放棄準備。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你負責校慶當日的聲音播放，原計劃只靠一部需連網的電腦。你想向團隊提出事前測試的離線副本和另一部可用裝置，不把「有後備」當成毋須檢查。用一至兩句英文建議安排。

examples.en: We should not have all our eggs in one basket by relying on one connected computer for the celebration. Let’s test an offline copy on a second device before the day.
examples.zh: 校慶播放不應只依靠一部連網電腦。讓我們在當日之前，在另一部裝置測試離線副本。

examples.en: I do not want us to have all our eggs in one basket if the computer loses its connection. Could we prepare a tested offline copy and check that another device can play it?
examples.zh: 如果電腦失去連線，我不想我們只有單一依靠。我們可否準備已測試的離線副本，並檢查另一部裝置能否播放？

writing.selfCheckZh: 提出真正可用且已測試的替代途徑，減少單一依賴；不把副本名稱或裝置數量本身當成功保證。

takeaways.en: The editor did not want to have all her eggs in one basket, so she sought permission for a second image while waiting for the first photographer’s reply.
takeaways.zh: 編輯不想只依賴單一選項，所以等第一位攝影師回覆時，也詢問另一張圖片的使用許可。

takeaways.en: By booking three venues, the theatre avoids putting all its eggs in one basket.
takeaways.zh: 劇院預訂三個場地，避免把所有希望押在同一選項上。
